chunks: Abū ʿAlī al-Ashʿarī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Thaʿlabah, from Sulaymān ibn Ṭarīf, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I heard him saying: Indeed, sin deprives the servant of sustenance.

key_terms.الذَّنْبَ: sin; an act of disobedience that brings spiritual and worldly harm
key_terms.الرِّزْقَ: sustenance; provision, livelihood, and blessings granted by Allah
key_terms.الْعَبْدَ: the servant; the human being as a servant of Allah
key_terms.يَحْرِمُ: deprives; prevents someone from receiving something beneficial

ai.seo_question: How do sins affect a person's sustenance in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that sins have worldly consequences in addition to spiritual harm. Among those consequences is being deprived of rizq, showing a moral connection between obedience to Allah and blessing in one’s livelihood.
